title: Name and vital statistics; family genealogy
description: The interviewer records Pearl's maiden name, nickname, birth date, and birthplace. Pearl provides detailed biographical information about her parents, siblings, husband, and children.

title: Education; farm skills; rural life; Canada years
description: Pearl discusses her eighth-grade education, quilting, and farm work. She compares rural and urban living and explains her family's move to Canada and her return to Idaho after her mother's death.

title: Meeting her husband; courtship; marriage
description: Pearl describes meeting Orville Choate at a community dance when she was young. She discusses their courtship, wedding, and their life together on the farm.

title: Schooling; childhood work; relationship with aunt and uncle
description: Pearl explains her rapid progress through school and her desire for further education. She describes living with her uncle and aunt, doing housework, and feeling like an outsider.

title: Starting the farm; marriage relationship; family life
description: Pearl discusses establishing the farm and her contentment with rural life. She describes her marriage, resolving disagreements, and her close relationship with her mother.

title: Childbirth experiences; family size; children's births
description: Pearl recounts difficult home births with her three daughters and her heart problems. She discusses wanting more children and the doctor's advice to stop after three.

title: Recreation; extension clubs; teaching daughters
description: Pearl describes her participation in the Grange and extension clubs. She discusses teaching her daughters domestic skills and their career choices.

title: Midwifery work; helping neighbors; birthing practices
description: Pearl explains her unpaid work as a midwife, assisting neighbors during births and illnesses. She describes traditional practices like the ten-day bed rest after childbirth.

title: Insurance; Depression; war years; community support
description: Pearl discusses acquiring life insurance and surviving the Depression and World War II. She describes rationing and community mutual aid during hard times.

title: Death customs; home funerals; changes in funeral practices
description: Pearl describes sitting up with the dead and preparing bodies at home before undertakers were common. She compares past and present funeral practices and costs.

title: Church preferences; religious experiences
description: Pearl discusses her church attendance at United Brethren and her preference for Baptist services. She describes emotional worship styles and her childhood religious training.

title: Church community; religious practices
description: Pearl describes the Dunkirk church and its traditional practices including long dresses, prayer veils, and baptism under the platform. She explains how the congregation evolved into a community church as people moved away, and expresses her preference for plain Bible preaching over ritualistic practices.

title: Reading material; television habits
description: Pearl lists the magazines the family subscribes to, including farm journals and Ladies Home Journal. She discusses watching television soap operas and evening programs like The Waltons and Gunsmoke, commenting on how realistic these portrayals are.

title: Family structure change; elderly care
description: Pearl reflects on how The Waltons portrays realistic family life from earlier eras when grandparents lived with family rather than in nursing homes. She notes how family life and farming have changed significantly over the generations.

title: Household appliances; modern conveniences
description: Pearl discusses modern appliances like washing machines and electric stoves, which she values highly while still keeping their old wood stove and conventional washing machine as backups.

title: Children's chores; family discipline
description: Pearl explains her approach to assigning household tasks by rotating chores among children so none became burdened with repetitive work. She describes how she and her husband maintained consistent discipline by supporting each other's decisions and discussing matters privately.

title: Youth recreation; family gatherings
description: Pearl describes what her children did for recreation, including Sunday school, dances, and movies in Garfield. She details how the family maintains traditions of birthday meals and holiday gatherings, with married daughters rotating Christmas visits between families.

title: Grandchildren; land values and farming
description: Pearl counts her grandchildren and great-grandchildren, then discusses the challenge of outsiders buying up large acreage at high prices. She recounts their own land purchases over the years and the dramatic increase in property values.

title: Farming history; farm succession
description: Pearl describes starting farming with horses when machinery was less expensive, working the land until age 67 before renting it out. She discusses the lack of family members able or willing to take over the farm operation.

title: Early marriage years; wedding story
description: Pearl recalls using dynamite boxes for furniture while waiting three months for their wedding gifts to arrive from the general store. She tells the story of getting married during scarlet fever quarantine, with the minister performing the ceremony outside on the porch to avoid contagion.
